chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two of them, peace be upon them, about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf while he was not in a state of ritual purity. He said: He should perform wudu (ablution) and repeat his tawaf; and if it was supererogatory, he should perform wudu (ablution) and pray two rak'ahs.

key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf that is legally required
key_terms.غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ: without being in a state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs tawaf without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding tawaf performed without ritual purity. It distinguishes between obligatory tawaf, which must be repeated after wudu (ablution), and supererogatory tawaf, for which wudu (ablution) is performed followed by two rak'ahs.
